examples.ko: 학원 등록비가 한 달에 십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The academy's registration fee is 100,000 won a month.
You have to pay the registration fee when you apply.
I paid the swimming pool registration fee by card.
This year the registration fee went up compared to last year.
The textbook cost is also included in the registration fee.

examples.ko: 이미 낸 등록비를 돌려받을 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can I get back the registration fee I already paid?

explain: 학원, 운동 시설, 동호회 같은 곳에 처음 등록할 때 내는 돈이에요. 대학교에서 내는 돈은 보통 '등록금'이라고 해요. 매달 내는 돈은 '수강료'나 '회비'처럼 따로 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the money you pay when first signing up for places like academies, gyms or clubs. What students pay at a university is usually called '등록금'. Monthly payments are often called '수강료' or '회비'.

examples.en: I volunteer at a nursing home every weekend.
In college, I volunteered abroad every vacation.
There are many people who volunteer for their neighbors.

examples.ko: 내일 같이 봉사할 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to volunteer with tomorrow.

examples.ko: 아이들에게 책을 읽어 주며 봉사하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to volunteer by reading books to children.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 사회에 봉사하면서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even when I'm older, I want to live serving society.

explain: 돈을 받지 않고 남을 돕는 일에 주로 써요. 보통 '봉사 활동을 하다'라고 말하고, 가게에서 손님을 대하는 일은 '서비스'라고 해요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to helping others without pay, and people often say '봉사 활동을 하다'. Treating customers in a shop is called '서비스' instead.

examples.ko: 저는 열 살 때 새어머니를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my stepmother when I was ten.
My stepmother cares for me like her own daughter.
My stepmother made me a delicious kimchi stew.
At first, talking with my stepmother felt awkward.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 새어머니가 나쁜 사람으로 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: In dramas, the stepmother is often shown as a bad person.
On Parents' Day this time, I gave flowers to my stepmother.

explain: '계모'라는 말도 있지만 부정적인 느낌이 강해서, 말할 때나 부를 때는 '새어머니'가 부드러워요. 아버지 쪽은 '새아버지'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '어머니'나 '엄마'라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: There is also the word '계모', but it carries a strong negative feeling, so '새어머니' is gentler when talking about her. The father's side is '새아버지'. When addressing her directly, people often just say '어머니' or '엄마'.

examples.en: I collect stamps as a hobby.
My younger sibling collected toys as a child.
I'm in the middle of collecting data for my paper.
I want to collect postcards while traveling.
We collected opinions with a survey and presented them.
I arranged the stamps I collected in an album.

explain: '모으다'가 일상 말이라서 돈·친구·사람은 '모으다'를 쓰고, '수집하다'는 취미나 자료·정보를 체계적으로 모을 때 써요. '돈을 모으다'는 되지만 '돈을 수집하다'는 어색해요. 물건을 수집하는 사람은 '수집가'라고 해요.
explain_en: '모으다' is the everyday word, so money or friends take 모으다, while 수집하다 is for collecting hobby items, materials or information in an organized way. '돈을 모으다' works, but '돈을 수집하다' sounds odd. A person who collects things is a '수집가'.

dis.h: collect systematically, as a hobby or data

p.n: 모으다 is plainer and everyday; it also covers saving money.

examples.en: I sent New Year greetings by text.
I will definitely start exercising in the new year.
The family gathered together to welcome the new year.

examples.ko: 신년의 첫날에는 가족과 함께 떡국을 먹어요.
examples.en: On the first day of the new year, we eat tteokguk with the family.
At the new year gathering, the boss gave a greeting.
When the new year comes, we make wishes.

explain: 신년 인사로는 '새해 복 많이 받으세요'라고 해요. '신년'은 한자어라서 격식 있는 글이나 방송에 잘 나오고, 대화에서는 '새해'를 더 많이 써요. '신년사', '신년회'처럼 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: The greeting is '새해 복 많이 받으세요'. '신년' is Sino-Korean, so it fits formal writing and broadcasts; in conversation '새해' is more common. It also attaches to words like '신년사' and '신년회'.

examples.ko: 한쪽 렌즈에 금이 가서 안경점에 갔어요.
examples.en: One lens cracked, so I went to the optician's.
My sunglasses lens got scratched, so I had it replaced at the optician's.

examples.ko: 집 근처 안경점이 오늘은 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The optician's near my home is closed today.

examples.ko: 안경점에서 시력을 재고 새 안경을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I had my eyesight tested and ordered new glasses at the optician's.

examples.ko: 안경점 사장님이 안경테를 친절하게 골라 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner of the optician's kindly helped me choose frames.
My glasses got loose, so I stopped by the optician's to have them adjusted.

explain: 안경을 맞추는 것뿐 아니라 렌즈를 갈거나 안경다리를 조이는 것도 안경점에서 해 줘요. 가게 이름에는 '안경원'이라는 말을 쓰는 곳도 있어요.
explain_en: Besides ordering glasses, you can also get lenses replaced or temples tightened at an '안경점'. Some shops use the name '안경원' instead.

examples.en: I put aloe on my sunburned skin.

examples.ko: 알로에는 물을 자주 주지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: Aloe does not need to be watered often.
I put an aloe pot by the window.

examples.ko: 알로에가 많이 자라서 큰 화분으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The aloe grew a lot, so I moved it to a bigger pot.
I bought aloe juice at the supermarket.
Cream made with aloe is gentle on the skin.

explain: 식물 이름이면서 주스나 화장품 재료 이름으로도 써요. 먹는 것은 '알로에 주스', 바르는 것은 '알로에 젤'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여요. 화분은 '키우다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is a plant name and also the name of an ingredient in juice and cosmetics. Words follow it, like '알로에 주스' for a drink and '알로에 젤' for something you apply. A potted plant goes with '키우다'.

examples.en: If you sit in the front row, you can see the stage well.
Shorter students stand in the front row.
I bought a front row ticket for the show at a high price.
The person in the front row raised their hand.
The front row is already full.
I could not hear from the back row, so I moved to the front row.

explain: 앞줄은 맨 앞의 줄을 말하고, '앞자리'는 앞쪽 자리들을 두루 말하는 느낌이에요. 반대말은 '뒷줄'이에요. 극장·교실·콘서트에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 앞줄 means the very first row, while '앞자리' loosely refers to the seats toward the front. The opposite is '뒷줄' (back row). It is common for theaters, classrooms, and concerts.

examples.en: I went to a campground with my family on the weekend.
I like this campground because the shower rooms are clean.
In summer, campground reservations fill up quickly.
We pitched a tent at the campground and grilled meat.
There is a valley stream near the campground, so it's cool.

examples.ko: 야영장 이용 요금은 하룻밤에 삼만 원이에요.
examples.en: The campground fee is thirty thousand won per night.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '캠핑장'이라고 더 자주 말하는 편이에요. 안내문이나 공식적인 글에서는 '야영장'이 많이 보여요. 두 말은 뜻이 같아요.
explain_en: In everyday conversation people tend to say '캠핑장' more. In notices and official writing you often see '야영장'. The two words mean the same thing.

examples.ko: 약방에서 붕대를 사다가 상처 난 곳에 감았어요.
examples.en: I bought a bandage at the drugstore and wrapped it around the wound.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 약방에서 감기약을 샀어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I bought cold medicine at the neighborhood drugstore.
My grandfather is old friends with the man at the drugstore.
Old drugstores were full of the smell of herbal medicine.
The drugstore is closed, so I plan to go tomorrow.

examples.ko: 요즘은 약방보다 약국이라는 말을 더 많이 써요.
examples.en: These days people say yakguk more than yakbang.

explain: 요즘은 보통 '약국'이라고 하고, '약방'은 옛날 느낌이나 한약을 파는 가게 느낌이 있어요. 지금 동네 가게를 말할 때는 '약국'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 어느 드라마에나 나오는 약방의 감초예요.
phrases.en: That actor is the one who shows up in every drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한약에 감초가 거의 늘 들어가는 데서 나온 말로, 어디에나 빠지지 않고 끼는 사람이나 물건을 말해요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓸 때가 많지만 참견하는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Coming from licorice root being added to almost every herbal remedy, it describes a person or thing that is part of everything. It is often positive but can also be used for someone who gets involved in everything.
phrases.en_equiv: a fixture; someone who's in everything

explain_en: Today people usually say '약국', while '약방' has an old-fashioned feel or suggests a shop selling herbal medicine. For a neighborhood shop today, '약국' sounds more natural.

examples.en: We did a restaurant role-play in class today.
I pair up with a friend and practice the role-play.
Thanks to role-plays, speaking became much easier.

examples.ko: 선생님은 역할극으로 주문하는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher taught us how to order through a role-play.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 역할극 발표를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our class is preparing a role-play presentation.
In the role-play, I took the customer part.

explain: 주로 학교나 학원 수업에서 상황을 정해 놓고 말해 보는 활동을 가리켜요. '역할극을 하다'라고 자주 말해요. 무대에서 하는 '연극'과는 달리 연습과 배움이 목적일 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to a classroom activity where students act out a set situation. People often say '역할극을 하다'. Unlike '연극' (a stage play), it is usually for practice and learning.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 시작한 그림을 드디어 완성했어요.
examples.en: I finally finished the painting I started in art class.

examples.ko: 이 보고서를 오늘 퇴근 전까지 완성해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to finish this report before I leave work today.

examples.ko: 주말에 가족과 큰 퍼즐을 같이 완성해요.
examples.en: On weekends I finish a big puzzle together with my family.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 내년 봄에 완성할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll complete this novel next spring.
I finished the dish and took a nice photo of it.
I showed my friend the finished work.

explain: '끝내다'는 어떤 일이든 멈출 때 쓰지만, '완성하다'는 그림·요리·보고서처럼 만들던 것이 다 만들어졌을 때만 써요. 그래서 수업이나 청소에는 '완성하다' 대신 '마치다', '끝내다'를 써요. 반대말은 '미완성'이고, 저절로 다 만들어졌다고 할 때는 '그림이 완성됐어요'처럼 '완성되다'를 써요.
explain_en: '끝내다' (end) works for any activity, but 완성하다 is only for things being made, such as a painting, a dish or a report, once they are fully done. For a class or cleaning, use '마치다' or '끝내다' instead. The opposite is '미완성' (unfinished), and when something simply ends up finished you say '완성되다', as in 'The painting got finished'.

p.n: 완료하다 is for tasks or procedures, so it is odd for a painting.

examples.ko: 위험물은 비행기에 가지고 탈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't bring hazardous materials onto a plane.

examples.ko: 위험물을 옮길 때는 특별히 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be especially careful when moving dangerous goods.

examples.ko: 이 창고에는 위험물이 많아서 불을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: There are many hazardous materials in this warehouse, so you must not use fire.

examples.ko: 위험물 표시가 있는 상자는 열지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't open boxes with a hazardous materials label.
I received safety training about hazardous materials.
It's classified as dangerous goods, so I can't send it by parcel.

explain: 공항, 택배, 공장의 안내문에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '위험한 물건'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요. '위험물 취급'처럼 뒤에 다른 말이 붙기도 해요.
explain_en: You often see this word in notices at airports, delivery services and factories. In everyday talk people often say '위험한 물건' instead. Other words can follow it, as in '위험물 취급' (handling hazardous materials).

examples.en: My parents run a business at the market.
I opened a shop with the money I earned from trading.
These days it's a hard time to run a business.
Since I started running a shop, the day passes really fast.
I learned how to do business from a young age.

examples.ko: 장사를 하려면 손님이 많은 곳이 좋아요.
examples.en: To run a shop, a place with many customers is good.

explain: 장사는 가게나 시장에서 물건을 사고파는 작은 규모의 일에 잘 어울려요. '사업하다'는 회사를 운영하는 더 큰 일이라는 느낌이 있어요. 가게가 잘될 때는 '장사가 잘돼요'라고 해요.
explain_en: 장사 suits the smaller trade of buying and selling at a shop or market. 사업하다 feels like running a bigger company. When a shop is doing well, you say 장사가 잘돼요.

examples.en: I do training every evening.
The training was so hard that I took a day off.

examples.ko: 새 직원 트레이닝은 이 주 동안 해요.
examples.en: The new staff training lasts two weeks.
I also want to join this training.
Training is important, but resting is important too.
I am building my stamina with training at home.

explain: 운동에는 '운동', 회사나 학교의 교육에는 '교육'을 쓰는 경우가 많아서 '트레이닝'은 조금 전문적인 느낌이 있어요. '트레이닝복', '트레이닝 바지'처럼 운동할 때 입는 옷 이름에도 나와요.
explain_en: Plain exercise is usually '운동' and workplace or school instruction is often '교육', so '트레이닝' sounds a bit specialized. It also appears in clothing names like '트레이닝복' and '트레이닝 바지'.

en: older brother's wife (said by a man)

examples.en: My older brother's wife is always kind to me.

examples.ko: 설날에 형수가 맛있는 전을 부쳐 주었어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year, my brother's wife made delicious pancakes.
I gave baby clothes to my brother's wife.
My brother and his wife moved into a new house.
I call my brother's wife by a respectful title.
My brother's wife's hometown is Busan.

explain: 남자가 형의 아내를 부르는 말이에요. 부를 때는 보통 '형수님'이라고 해요. 누나의 남편은 '매형'으로 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is what a man calls his older brother's wife. When addressing her, you usually say 형수님. An older sister's husband is a separate term, 매형.
